claim.why_it_matters: The indentation that carries the element hierarchy is scrambled: the ALL option of ZEROS... sits at the depth of Figurative constants, Symbolic-character is nested deeper than the figurative constants instead of beside Figurative constants, ALL literal and Nonnumeric literals are shallower than their siblings, and Numeric literals is no longer under Literals, so which entry each ALL option qualifies cannot be read from the markdown.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 32 (I-12, Nucleus element summary) at 300 dpi. Printed indentation: Figurative constants, Symbolic-character and ALL literal all start at one column (siblings under Special purpose words). ZERO... and ZEROS... sit one step deeper, and each of their ALL options one step deeper again. The ALL option under Symbolic-character is deeper than Symbolic-character. Literals is at the outer level, with Numeric and Nonnumeric literals both one step in. page-32.md lines 11-21 give   counts Figurative 5, ZERO 6, ALL 7, ZEROS 6, ALL 5, Symbolic 8, ALL 5, ALL literal 1, Literals 2, Numeric 2, Nonnumeric 1. So in the markdown, the ALL option under ZEROS is at the depth of Figurative constants. Symbolic-character is nested below the ZEROS row, not beside Figurative constants, and its ALL option is shallower than it. ALL literal is at depth 1, Numeric literals is level with Literals, and Nonnumeric literals is shallower than Literals. The claim quotes both sources correctly. In this table, indentation alone shows which entry each ALL option and literal row belongs to, so the transcription changes the meaning. This is not line wrapping or page furniture. The table is an informative level summary, which limits the impact.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed. One more detail: in the PDF, the ALL option under Symbolic-character is indented deeper than Symbolic-character, but the markdown puts it shallower (5 versus 8  ).
